messages.author: 4bfedef6037d567c
messages.subject: Thresold  for stepwiseqtl
parts:
Hi! 

I use the function stepwiseqtl() to do a MQM on the population that I study. 
 Before I did that :

operm1 <- vector("list")
for (i in phes)
{
  operm1[[i]] <- scantwopermhk(cross.calc, pheno.col = i, n.perm=1,
                               addcovar=NULL, weights=NULL, 
                               batchsize = 1000, verbose=FALSE)
}

to obatin the thresold with 1000 permutation for each phneotype.  Sometime I change n.perm = 10 and batchsize = 100 to obtain 1000 permutation.
Is this OK? Do I really obtain 1000 permutations? 

Than I use this command 

stepwise_cross_list = list()
t = 1
for (i in names(cross.calc[["pheno"]])) {
  cross_pen <- calc.penalties(operm1[[i]], alpha=.05)
  stepwise_cross <- stepwiseqtl(cross.calc, method="hk", model="normal", pheno.col= i, max.qtl=5, covar=NULL,
                                penalties = cross_pen,scan.pairs=FALSE, additive.only=T,keeplodprofile=TRUE,
                                keeptrace=TRUE, refine.locations=TRUE, verbose=TRUE, incl.markers= T)

Does stepwiseqtl really include my thresold in the analysis? Or did I make a mistake? Because I didn't precise If I wanted the main, the heavy or the light one? 
Does this matter? I tested with penalties = cross_pen1.05[1:2] but I have the same result when I obtain my output.
 Because I am about to publish but I started to be afraid that the thresold wasn't right...

Thank you for the reply.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Thresold for stepwiseqtl
parts:
If you use n.perm=1 then it doesn't matter what batchsize is, you'll just get a single permutation replicate.
batchsize takes the n.perm permutations and breaks them into groups and analyses them together, but if batchsize > n.perm then it's the same as if batchsize=n.perm.

Look at the permutation output to make sure they look reasonable; plot histograms.

calc.penalties calculates the main, heavy, and light penalties, and stepwise() makes use of them.

karl
